trust_decision.summary: The filesystem template loader decides whether a requested template path is inside the configured basepath root: resolve() must only return identifiers under basepath, and it is the sole producer of identifiers for the fs reads in load(). At the pinned commit resolve() returns path.resolve(from, to) unconditionally, with no root check, and all four frontends (native, django, jinja2, twig) and every include/extends/import/from/compileFile/renderFile route funnel through this one resolver.

landing_point.why: The summary names include/extends path traversal, so a summary-only reader starts at the tag that turns a template path expression into a template load; each of the four frontends has its own include/extends tag (swig-core has none), so the named mechanism appears to live in four places while the actual decision is one package down in the shared loader at filesystem.js:28.

fix_sites.entry_point: swig.loaders.fs(basepath).resolve / .load, reached by swig.compileFile / compileFileAsync / renderFile / renderFileAsync and by {% include %} / {% extends %} / {% import %} / {% from %} at render time
fix_sites.module_kind: shared loader in the core package (one layer below all four frontends; the root lib/loaders/filesystem.js is a one-line re-export of it)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the no-basepath branch alone by arguing it has no declared root: the report's example and the published fix both assume a basepath, and `../` includes/extends across a template tree are the normal, shipped case under the default loader (tests/cases/extends_tests/extends_3.test.html:1), so only the basepath branch reads as 'the bug'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Parent-relative `../` extends/include must keep working under the default filesystem loader (no basepath), where resolution is relative to the including file's directory; a fix that confines every resolve() to a root also breaks the template trees the project ships as test fixtures.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: tests/cases/extends_tests/extends_3.test.html:1 and tests/cases/extends_layouts/extends_include.html:2, both compiled through the default no-basepath loader by tests/templates.test.js:63

O6_input_shapes: literal relative traversal string, e.g. '../../../etc/passwd' and '../secret.txt' (fix.diff:66-68)
path supplied by an untrusted runtime local, `{% include leak %}` with locals {leak: '../secret.txt'} (fix.diff:103-106)
sibling directory sharing the root's name prefix, '../views-secret/x.html' (fix.diff:69-70)
caller-supplied `from` argument that cannot widen the root (fix.diff:71-72)
the root directory itself as target, '.' (fix.diff:64-65)
opt-out shape: third factory argument allowOutsideRoot = true restores pre-fix resolution (fix.diff:75-83)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Default filesystem loader with no basepath: resolve() takes the `from`/process.cwd() branch and applies no confinement, so `{% include leak %}` (or extends/import) with an untrusted absolute path such as '/etc/passwd', or a path that climbs out of the template tree, is read from disk by the same load() sink.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the report's example and the fix both assume a basepath, so the no-basepath branch reads as having no declared root at all; and the shipped fixtures rely on `../` includes/extends with the default loader, so confining this branch looks like it would break legitimate templates (leaving the absolute-path case wide open).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: adjacent branch of the same resolver, but the report never mentions basepath, so nothing points at it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: memory loader resolve() is a near-copy of the fs loader's, with the same basepath branch and no confinement
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the two loaders implement one published contract with identical resolve bodies (only the fallback root differs), so a maintainer hardening loader paths would mirror the check here to keep the contract consistent

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a chroot/prefixing loader built from the documented custom-loader example whose resolve is plain path.resolve(from, to)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the loader docs publish exactly this shape as the way to write a loader, so a maintainer offering 'read templates only from this prefix' would add the check in a new loader of this form

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a per-call root option on getTemplate/compileFileAsync (Express-style view root) that re-resolves the entry path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the helper already accepts a per-call resolveFrom option it could extend, and view engines commonly take a per-call root

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal: arbitrary local file read through template include/extends/import paths

O10_build.toolchain: npm install for workspaces + devDeps (esbuild, eslint, terser, express); `make test` runs node --test with tests/lib/mocha-compat.js; `make build` produces the browser bundle
O10_build.project_tests: tests/loaders.test.js (fs and memory loader API, including a basepath render), tests/templates.test.js (walks tests/cases/** and compiles every *.test.html with the default loader, including parent-relative extends), tests/tags/include.test.js, tests/tags/extend.test.js, tests/async/*; no path-confinement or traversal tests exist at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a cheap string test inside resolve() only when basepath is set (a raw `startsWith(basepath)` prefix check or a `to.indexOf('..') !== -1` throw), which lets a sibling dir with the same name prefix through, breaks relative basepaths, and leaves the no-basepath and absolute-path routes open.

The published fix compares an absolute `resolved` against path.normalize(basepath) (fix.diff:39-40). A relative basepath such as swig.loaders.fs('views') would therefore reject every path; not confirmed by execution, and no pinned test uses a relative basepath (tests/loaders.test.js:96,102 both use __dirname).

Whether the no-basepath O8 route can be closed without breaking tests/cases/extends_tests/* was reasoned from the fixtures only, not executed; the fair form looks like rejecting absolute include paths when no basepath is configured.
